newsitem.title: JAPAN: Glaxo Wellcome seen making inroads in Japan market.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome seen making inroads in Japan market.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc's move to take full control of its joint venture in Japan will enable the leading pharmaceutical company to make more inroads into the Japanese market, analysts say.

"By cutting off outside influence, Glaxo Wellcome will gain a free hand in making aggressive expansion moves in Japan," said Yoshihiko Yamamoto, director of equity research at Salomon Brothers Asia Ltd.
He said Glaxo Wellcome's business in Japan has been tiny in relation to its strong global presence. The firm is the world's largest drug maker in terms of sales.

In the Japanese market, Glaxo Wellcome's combined sales, through licensing and joint ventures, only ranked 15th in the year ended on June 30, said a spokesman for Nippon Glaxo, its joint venture with Shin Nihon Jitsugyo Ltd in Japan.

Salomon's Yamamoto said Glaxo Wellcome may buy a local drug maker in the future. "In an effort to strengthen marketing in Japan, Glaxo Wellcome may choose to buy a local drug maker, which could induce a long-awaited reorganisation of Japan's pharmaceutical industry."
Glaxo Wellcome announced last week that it would turn Nippon Glaxo into a wholly owned subsidiary.
It will buy Shin Nihon's 50 percent stake for 66 billion yen ($584 million) before the end of the year, and will also pay Shin Nihon 1.38 billion yen ($12.2 million) in lieu of dividends for 1996.
Some analysts said Glaxo Wellcome may be paying too much for the stake, as the joint venture has total assets of 30.7 billion yen ($271 million).
The company said when it announced the move that "the acquisition...provides a platform for the optimisation of Glaxo Wellcome's business in Japan, the world's second-largest pharmaceutical market".

Analysts and industry officials said that despite a series of government measures to cut medical spending, the Japanese market is looking increasingly attractive for foreign drug makers as the nation's ageing population and their health needs are expected to lead to increased demand for medicines.
An official at the Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association said many foreign drug makers have recently begun marketing their products on their own rather than rely on Japanese companies.
Nippon Glaxo posted 51 billion yen ($451 million) in sales in the year to June 30, up from 43 billion yen ($380 million) in the previous year.
Glaxo Wellcome also has a joint venture with Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd in Japan called Nippon Wellcome KK. Glaxo Wellcome holds a majority 55 percent stake in that firm. ($1=113 yen)
